items.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: they don’t take the time out to study Noro Morales, Tito Puente, Machito, you know the basic things.

ctx.x: In other words you fit in first.

Right. First. And then you’ve got to experiment. Like you go through the doors, see what’s happening in there, you know you can walk through further, say hi, so you’re kind of introducing yourself to each song and each style. So this is why we have — we also, you know we go out into studying this full, to the full extent of each genre. Latin people. So and it dawns on me why not, when the American people play a Latin tune, they won’t go out and study these laws — the basics — a little tumbao on the piano, a…
So is studying the music mostly an oral thing listening to recordings?
